findings.description: Long-lived AWS access-key credentials are embedded in EC2 user data, placing them in Terraform source/state and making them readable through instance/user-data access paths. Anyone obtaining these credentials can authenticate as the associated IAM principal until they are revoked or rotated.

No metadata_options configuration requires IMDSv2, so the instance can permit IMDSv1. A server-side request forgery flaw on the host could retrieve instance-profile credentials from the metadata service if an instance profile is later attached.

The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key, so its encryption depends on an external account-level default and is not enforced by this configuration. Data written to this volume may therefore be stored unencrypted.

This snapshot is created from an EBS volume whose encryption is not enforced; EBS snapshots inherit the source volume's encryption state. It can therefore preserve the attached volume's data without encryption at rest.
TCP/22 is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administration to every internet host. This enables broad scanning, brute-force, and exploitation attempts against the instance.
All protocols and ports are allowed to 0.0.0.0/0 for egress. A compromised web host can use this unrestricted path for command-and-control or data exfiltration.

The flow-log bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so encryption at rest is not enforced by Terraform. Network-flow records written to this bucket may be stored without the intended encryption control.
